title: w0m client-import registry (T182)
description: Declares the projects the client-import inventory measures, and which one carries the contract. Validated so the registry itself cannot become the divergent, unread schema this ticket exists to fix.

contract_file.description: Path, relative to each project root, of the declaration file diffed across projects.

projects.description: At least two: the estate plus one client. A single-entry registry would make the diff vacuous.

root.description: Path relative to the estate root (…/@wom). May resolve outside it. SIMPLE mode (no `repos`): this MUST be a git repo root — the original rule, unchanged. WORKSPACE mode (`repos` present): this is the PROJECT root, a parent folder that need not be a repo itself; the repos under it carry the git-root guarantee instead. T268.

repos.description: WORKSPACE mode. Logical name -> path relative to this project's `root`, the same vocabulary `.w0m/sdlc.json` already uses for w0m's own seven repos. Presence of this key IS the mode — there is deliberately no separate `mode` field, because a flag can disagree with the shape it describes. EVERY entry must resolve to a git repo ROOT: the hard-fail simple mode applies to `root` moves here, it is not relaxed.

canonical_repo.description: WORKSPACE mode, required with `repos`. Where the project's `.w0m/` contract lives. Two legal forms: a key of `repos` (the contract sits in that repo — w0m uses "wom7web", whose path wom7api/scripts/supabase_limits.py resolves from a hardcoded location), or "." meaning the WORKSPACE ROOT itself. The second form exists because a client's only app repo may not be ours — BridgeRoad's single repo is a third-party org's, and putting our contract there is what T265 AC8 forbids. 🔴 "." is legal ONLY when the workspace root is itself a git repo root. T268 AC7 made 'configuration at an untracked parent' (D32) inexpressible by requiring the contract inside a declared repo; allowing the root because it IS a repo we own is a different claim from allowing an untracked parent, and client_inventory hard-fails the latter by name. ⚠️ OPTIONAL for role 'half-managed', where its ABSENCE means the project has NO w0m contract at all — we place none, because we write nothing to it. That is NOT D32: D32 is configuration that EXISTS while versioned nowhere; this is configuration that does not exist by decision. Conflating them would let 'we left our config lying in someone's directory' hide behind 'we deliberately have none'.

tier_reason.description: Required for role 'half-managed'. WHY this project is not fully managed — ownership, who runs it, what the estate deliberately does not reach. A tier without a reason degrades into a status nobody can question; `enabled: false` already reads as 'paused', and this must not become a second such value. Printed by client-inventory beside the project.

services.description: T299 AC3 — Per-project service switches overriding role defaults. Each override MUST explicitly declare 'enabled' and a 'reason' (minLength: 20).

reason.description: Why this service is overridden for this specific project (min 20 chars). An unexplained override degrades into an unexaminable exception.

repo_identities.description: Per-repo identity overrides in workspace mode (keyed by repo name).

org_slug.description: T272 — Canonical slug in public.orgs when this client project has a portal organization.

project_slug.description: T272 — Canonical slug in public.projects when this client project has a portal project row.

external_services.description: T272 AC1/AC3/AC6 — Declared external and platform services used by this client project.

state_surface_candidates.description: Agent-maintained files whose size is reported per project (T177/T174 linkage). Reported, never judged — the threshold belongs to the profile gate, not the inventory.

tiers.description: T265 AC2 — per-tier IN/OUT decisions for every governance surface, keyed by role name. Tier names are constrained to the SAME definition the `role` property uses, so a tier cannot be defined for a role that does not exist, and adding a role cannot silently leave its tier unschema'd. ⚠️ COMPLETENESS against the estate contract stays with client_inventory: the contract's key set is data read at runtime, and a schema cannot know it.

services.description: T299 AC3 — Capability families and services w0m provides. Service names form the canonical vocabulary for role defaults and per-project switches.

roles.description: T299 AC2 — Canonical governance roles supplying default service switches. Every role must decide every declared service.

reason.description: Why this service is enabled or disabled by default for this role.

runtime.description: T297 AC1/AC2/AC3 — Where the project executes. Absence is NOT permitted (no default to 'host'). 🔴 AC3 boundary rule: estate gates (preflight, linters, tests, security probes) inspect only macOS host paths and do NOT reach inside guest VMs. A project inside a guest is therefore ungoverned from the host's point of view, and declaring runtime: tart-* makes this visible rather than implying coverage.

substrate.description: host — runs directly on macOS host. tart-linux — runs inside a Linux Tart VM (e.g. Ubuntu 26.04). tart-macos — runs inside a macOS Tart VM (limited to 2 per host by kernel cap).

guest_name.description: Name of the local Tart VM instance (e.g. 'w0m-bridgeroad', 'evercred'). Expected for tart-* runtimes so tooling can verify its presence via tart list (AC4).

role.description: w0m (formerly estate, T299 AC1) — the core estate workspace whose .w0m/sdlc.json IS the contract; exactly one required. managed (formerly client, T299 AC2) — fully managed project: full w0m governance, ticketing, and delivery pipeline. self-managed (formerly half-managed, T299 AC7) — external client-governed project: skills, tools, and SDLC apply; ticketing, deploys, and write access do not. on-prem — client project hosted on on-premise hardware.

vcs.description: T338 — OPTIONAL. Reuses the exact vocabulary `.w0m/sdlc.json` already defines for `vcs` (see `.w0m/README.md`) rather than inventing a second shape for the same fact. Absence means the link is not yet recorded here, not that the project has no repo — a project's own `.w0m/sdlc.json` (when it has one) remains the primary source; this field exists so the estate-level registry can show the link without opening every client's own config.

repo.description: `owner/name`, verified against the actual remote (`git remote -v` / `gh repo view`) — not copied from a project's own possibly-stale config.

surface.description: One governance surface, decided. `status` is the decision; `reason` is why. Both required: a surface listed without a decision is indistinguishable from one nobody considered, which is the state this tier system exists to end.

status.description: in — w0m governs this surface for the tier. out — it does not.

reason.description: Why. Deliberately short-friendly: real entries include "Tools." and "Ticketing.", which classify rather than argue and are the right length for a per-surface label. The bar only rejects empty and one-character values — an unexplained decision, not a terse one.

surface_map.description: Surface name -> decision. Must not be empty: an empty map reads as 'every surface decided' while deciding nothing.

definition.description: What the tier means in one paragraph, long enough to be a claim someone can disagree with.

identity.description: Declared developer or agent identity for git commits, SSH transport, and GitHub CLI (T300).

git_user_name.description: The expected git user.name (e.g. 'Aleksei Tcelishchev' or 'Elena Shatalova').

ssh_key.description: Filesystem path or pointer to SSH key (e.g. '~/.ssh/id_rsa'), NEVER private key content.

gh_account.description: GitHub username active for CLI operations.

external_service.description: T272 AC1/AC3/AC6 — Declared external or platform service used by a client project, referencing canonical service keys and stating reachability and cost attribution.

external_reason.description: Required when reachability is 'external' (renders as 'managed outside w0m' in CP, T272 AC1).

knowledge_hub.description: T284 AC1/AC5 — Declared client-facing knowledge hub corpus boundary. Maps a client org/project to its explicit vault_slug, corpus_root (relative to estate root), allowed_prefixes, and denied_prefixes so client document boundaries are DATA, never inferred from directory names.

allOf._comment: If any project claims the half-managed or self-managed tier, the tier must be defined. Otherwise a project can sit in a tier whose obligations are written nowhere.
